title: Read the label map
spec: Given loader labels 0 or 1, return integer 1 for malignant (original 0), else 0. Reject other labels.
explanation: Equality creates a Boolean mask; converting it to integer gives 1/0. The explicit map is necessary because numeric label order is not universal.

title: Count errors
spec: For aligned nonempty binary vectors return (true negatives,false positives,false negatives,true positives).
explanation: Count each actual/predicted pair separately; do not swap the row meaning and column meaning.

title: Calculate balanced accuracy
spec: For aligned binary vectors with both actual classes present, average recall for class 0 and class 1.
explanation: Each actual class contributes one recall regardless of how many rows belong to it. This does not certify clinical usefulness.

title: Use fitted scaling
spec: Standardize a finite 2-D matrix using supplied training means and positive scales. Do not calculate new means.
explanation: The training transformation is frozen. Recalculating it on the test query would change the model definition.

title: Choose nearby reference points
spec: Return indices of the k nearest reference points to a query using Euclidean distance; preserve input order on ties.
explanation: Distance selects neighbors; sorting indices preserves the link back to the training rows. The tie convention differs explicitly from the production teaching descriptor’s coordinate-based tie rule.

title: Filter finite lifetimes
spec: Given an n-by-2 birth/death array, return death-birth for finite positive-lifetime intervals only.
solution:
def finite_lifetimes(diagram):
    a=np.asarray(diagram,float).reshape(-1,2)
    valid=np.isfinite(a).all(axis=1)&(a[:,1]>a[:,0])
    return a[valid,1]-a[valid,0]
explanation: Essential classes need separate handling. Silently averaging infinity is not a meaningful finite persistence statistic.

title: Compute MAE
spec: Return mean absolute error for aligned nonempty finite vectors.
explanation: Absolute value removes the direction of error; averaging retains the response unit but can hide extreme failures.

title: Keep signed residuals
spec: Return observed minus predicted; the sign convention must be explicit.
explanation: A positive residual under this convention means the prediction was too low. Another convention is possible only when declared.

title: Leave one row out
spec: Return all integer indices from 0 to n-1 except the specified omitted index.
explanation: The scaler and model must both be refit on these indices, not only the model.

title: Lag within an entity
spec: Sort a table by firm and year and add lag_invest from the previous row within the same firm. Keep first records missing.
solution:
def lag_investment(table):
    result=table.sort_values(['firm','year']).copy()
    result['lag_invest']=result.groupby('firm')['invest'].shift(1)
    return result
checks:
t=pd.DataFrame({'firm':['A','B','A','B'],'year':[1,1,2,2],'invest':[10,90,20,80]})
r=lag_investment(t)
assert r.loc[2,'lag_invest']==10 and r.loc[3,'lag_invest']==90
assert r.loc[[0,1],'lag_invest'].isna().all()
explanation: Group boundaries are information boundaries. A global shift would mix different companies.

title: Enforce a cutoff
spec: Return indices with timestamp strictly earlier than the supplied decision cutoff.
solution:
def before_cutoff(times,cutoff):
    return np.flatnonzero(np.asarray(times)<cutoff)
explanation: Strictly earlier differs from earlier-or-equal. Decide how simultaneous measurements become available.

title: Find shared entities
spec: Return the set of entities appearing in both partitions.
solution:
def shared_entities(first,second):
    return set(first)&set(second)
explanation: Entity overlap can be acceptable for future-known-firm evaluation but invalid for a new-firm claim.

title: Preserve a missingness mask
spec: For a vector and positive window length, return starting indices of finite contiguous windows. This task checks rows only; time-spacing validation is a separate obligation.
explanation: A finite contiguous row window is necessary but not sufficient: real time gaps must also be checked.

title: Separate past and target
spec: For a finite vector make length-L feature windows and one-step targets. Return (x,y), including correctly shaped empty arrays.
explanation: The target is not included in its own features. Reading later true observations for later predictions is observed-history evaluation.

title: Check the entire support
spec: Return whether every integer index from start through target inclusive belongs to the allowed partition.
explanation: Checking only the final target misses leakage through an earlier feature or an intermediate observation.

title: Convert units explicitly
spec: Convert annual volumes expressed in 10^8 cubic metres to cubic metres. Do not call the output a rate.
solution:
def volume_in_cubic_metres(source_volume):
    return np.asarray(source_volume,float)*1e8
explanation: The conversion changes representation, not information about peaks or subannual timing.

title: Score a candidate split
spec: For a finite vector and split k with two nonempty segments, return the within-segment squared error around each segment mean.
explanation: Minimizing this across many k is a search; the selected minimum is not automatically a significance test.

title: Divide by the actual elapsed time
spec: Return successive finite-difference rates for aligned finite values and strictly increasing times.
explanation: A difference in annual volume per year is not the instantaneous river-discharge signal. Units propagate through the calculation.

title: Respect calendar order
spec: Given YEAR and JAN..DEC columns, return a 1-D vector in year-sorted calendar order.
explanation: Column names are not alphabetically ordered times; the explicit month sequence preserves meaning.

title: Fit only a supplied reference period
spec: For finite values and corresponding month labels 1..12, return twelve monthly means; require all months.
explanation: Which rows you pass determines the fitted climatology. The function cannot infer the training boundary for you.

title: Compute anomalies against a fixed baseline
spec: Subtract each value’s month-specific mean from a supplied length-12 reference.
explanation: A positive anomaly is relative to a declared baseline, not an absolute category of climate behavior.

title: Recover one selected mode per person
spec: Validate four modes and one selected alternative per individual, then return a Series of selected modes indexed by individual.
explanation: Four alternative rows contain one decision. Invalid choice sets must not silently create extra labels.

title: Build a cheapest-mode baseline
spec: Given an n-by-4 finite cost matrix ordered air/train/bus/car, return mode codes1..4; choose the first mode on ties.
explanation: A baseline embodies a simple assumption; it is not a claim that all people minimize ticket price.

title: Check disjoint travelers
spec: Return True precisely when the two identifier collections share no member.
solution:
def groups_disjoint(train_ids,test_ids):
    return not bool(set(train_ids)&set(test_ids))
explanation: Apply the same principle to athletes, patients and experiment runs. Disjoint rows alone do not establish disjoint entities.
